# Link

A text link (D119): the accent colour, underlined at rest, never marked by colour alone. Its rules are the `.psi-link` utility in utilities.css, which `Link` applies. With `href` it renders the anchor. Without, a router app passes its own link as the only child, and `Link` clones it to add the class and, with `current`, `aria-current="page"`, as `NavItem` does (D93). In that form, `Link`'s other anchor props and `ref` are not applied: put them on your link. The font is inherited, so a standalone link sits in a `Text`. Inside a `NavItem`, pass your router link itself, not `Link`: the utility layer would draw a text link in the nav. For an action that should look like a button, use `Button href`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | — | no | Render the anchor yourself: `<a href>` with `children` as its text. Router apps leave it out and pass their own link as the only child. |
| `current` | `boolean` | — | no | Mark the link as the current page (`aria-current="page"`): on the anchor `href` renders, or on the single element you pass as a child. Without `current`, a child's own `aria-current` is left alone. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | yes | With `href`: the link's text. Without: one link element, your router's. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | — | no | Forwarded ref to the anchor `href` renders. With a child link, put the ref on your link. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS class name(s) merged onto the component's root element. |

## Keyboard & assistive tech

| Keys | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Tab | Takes focus like any link and draws the shared focus ring (:focus-visible). |
| Enter | Follows the link. Your router's own link handles it when you pass one as the child. |

A native anchor (D119), either the one Link renders from href or your router's link passed as the only child. Underlined at rest, so it is never told from the text around it by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the accent scores about 2:1 against body text. current sets aria-current="page", drawn as medium-weight text with no underline. Psi adds no target or rel and no new-tab marker; if a link opens a new tab, say so in its text.

## Theming

Override `--psi-link-*` custom properties at any scope; interactive states derive automatically (L - 0.04 hover, L - 0.08 active).



## Rules

- One accent per visual group; everything else neutral or ghost.
- danger only for actions with real consequences.
- Sizes are px numbers (24|32|40|48), never S/M/L.
- Typography tokens are --psi-text-{size}-{lineHeight}-{weight}.
- Override component tokens (--psi-{component}-*), not semantic tokens, for one-off theming.
- --psi-button-font overrides button typography across all sizes (documented D34 override; ember → mono).
- Wrap labeled form controls in Field — label association, description/error line, aria-describedby and aria-invalid come wired; don't hand-roll label+message rows.
- Field is for a control with a *visible* label. A toolbar filter control named by aria-label or placeholder takes neither a Field nor a hand-rolled label row — compare filter-toolbar (no labels) with table-pagination ("Rows per page" visible, so Field). Filters with visible labels submitted together by a Find button are filter-form: a Toolbar as="form" align="start" of Fields with one-line labels, where a field's error line is the Field's own and hangs below its control (D87, D92).
- Label beside its control: <Field labelPosition="start"> for one field in a toolbar or pager (keep Toolbar align="center"); <FieldStack labelPosition="start"> for a form whose labels share one column, as wide as the longest label up to --psi-field-label-max-width, stacking below 480px of the form's width. A theme sets --psi-field-label-align: end to put labels against their controls (D115).
- Use Dialog for blocking modal flows — title/footer slots, dismissible gate; danger stays on the footer Buttons, one accent per group.
- Text links are Link (React) or the .psi-link class on any <a>: accent colour, underlined at rest, never by colour alone (D119). A router app passes its own link as Link's only child. Button href is for an action that should look like a button. Inside a NavItem, pass your router link itself, not Link.
